Assessment for a self-hosted multi-node substrate: it must replace per-process identity with (1) a stable operator-controlled CA/certificate with configurable SANs and wildcards and an optional plain-HTTP internal listener, (2) operator-supplied fixed credentials shared by all nodes, (3) one configurable advertised public endpoint plus forwarded-header policy that every minted URL uses, so no SDK can be pointed at real AWS or at loopback, (4) a durable versioned replicated state plane instead of one InMemoryEngine, (5) reproducible signed multi-arch packaging with a catalog whose versions map to real filenames and language-ecosystem wrappers, (6) telemetry off by default (or DNT and a local sink), (7) bundled per-Region and CloudFormation availability checks, (8) embedded-mode feature gating and cross-platform CI, and (9) a cluster configuration surface (node id, peers, shared CA/keys, node-aware readiness) with docs, contribution path and CI examples. All 13 findings are open divergences; nothing here establishes AWS parity, no fix was applied, and no fix design was validated at runtime. UNVERIFIED claims are marked explicitly per finding and in gaps.

findings.claim: The emulator generates one self-signed certificate per process whose SANs are only localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and IP literals derived from the bind address; there is no --tls-san, no certificate/key file input, no plain-HTTP data port, and no stable CA. Containers or pods reaching the emulator by service name cannot verify the hostname, and every restart rotates the CA and invalidates trust stores that were baked into an image or read once by a long-running process.
findings.root_cause: rcgen::generate_simple_self_signed is called with a hard-coded name list inside a process-global OnceLock whose names are fixed by the first call; the CLI parses no TLS options; the production data listener is rustls-only; ca.pem and truststore.p12 are written from that per-process certificate at startup and removed by an RAII guard on clean stop.
evidence: gh#23 (open, 'Containers can't reach the emulator by service name: the TLS certificate covers only localhost and 127.0.0.1'): reports the exact SAN list 'DNS:localhost, IP Address:127.0.0.1, IP Address:0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1', says a shared ca.pem still fails hostname verification for https://aws:9297, and has 5 comments covering Compose, GitHub Actions service containers, Kubernetes/ACK controllers, long-running Node watch-mode processes, browser/OS trust stores, Cognito token issuers, and S3 Control's 000000000000.localhost subdomain.

findings.claim: With --auth on, the emulator mints a random key pair per process, writes it to $HOME/.aws/emulator/<port>/emulator_credentials (mode 0600, removed on clean stop), and accepts no operator-supplied key pair. Sibling containers must share the emulator's HOME volume and wait for the file, and every restart re-keys them. The only practical workaround, --auth off, removes SigV4 verification entirely, so a tampered presigned URL is served 200 instead of 403.
findings.root_cause: SigV4Authenticator::for_this_process is a OnceLock of random hex strings; write_credentials_file is called at startup whenever the authenticator was registered and returns an EmulatorFile guard that deletes the file on drop. The CLI has no --access-key-id/--secret-access-key and no equivalent env vars; authentication is a process-wide AtomicBool that gates all registered authenticators.
evidence: gh#566 (open, 'Fixed access keys with request authentication on (--auth on), for containers that start with the emulator'): asks for --access-key-id/--secret-access-key or EMULATOR_ACCESS_KEY_ID/EMULATOR_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, or a documented fixed test pair; says the practical workaround is --auth off, after which a presigned URL with a changed signature is served 200. It reports test/test refused with InvalidClientTokenId and a changed-signature presigned GET returning 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch on 1.0.523.

gh#23 comments: ACK/Crossplane controllers read credentials from a Kubernetes Secret that must be rebuilt after every restart; long-running Node processes get AccessDenied after rotation; a per-branch Kubernetes preview environment needs fixed credentials or 'accept any non-empty ones ... but with SigV4 still on'.

findings.claim: The emulator has no configurable public endpoint. Its own published config hardcodes region = us-east-1 and endpoint_url = https://127.0.0.1:<port> even when bound 0.0.0.0, while several API responses mint addresses on real AWS hosts that the emulator does not serve (SQS QueueUrl is the clearest case) or on 127.0.0.1:<port> (ALB, CloudFront, RDS). An SDK that follows a returned address can leave the sandbox and send signed requests to real AWS; a client on another node cannot connect at all.
findings.root_cause: There is one request-independent endpoint concept: dialable_host() maps a wildcard bind back to loopback and shared_config_text() emits that value. Individual services build URLs from hardcoded DNS suffixes or from per-run listener sockets. A fidelity fix moved SQS from the listener socket to the AWS hostname form, which satisfies a wire recording but breaks the endpoint contract; no X-Forwarded-Proto/Host or advertised-URL setting exists to reconcile the two.
evidence: vendor/server/src/lib.rs:1261-1264 (endpoint_url = listeners::url_for(SocketAddr::new(client_host, port))), :1371-1377 (dialable_host maps an unspecified bind to loopback), :1403-1408 (shared_config_text hardcodes 'region = us-east-1' and that endpoint_url), :1269-1275 (one health route on the same HTTPS port); vendor/server/src/listeners.rs:749-750 url_for always emits https://.

findings.claim: All emulated service state lives in one process's InMemoryEngine type-map; there is no --data-dir, no snapshot/restore, no shared state backend and no replication. A restart — documented as the only way to reset state — discards every resource, and a crash or container memory eviction loses it too. A multi-node substrate therefore has no state plane to share.
findings.root_cause: The standalone and embedded entry points each construct one Arc<InMemoryEngine::new()>; InMemoryEngine.states is a Mutex<HashMap<TypeId, Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>>>; RunOptions has no persistence field. The only durable database in the tree is the telemetry outbox (rusqlite); service SQL engines are opened in memory.
evidence: gh#20 (open, 'Add persistence to maintain data across restarts') and its 4 comments: S3/SNS/SQS multi-step pipelines; Cognito user pool ids, app client ids, users and signing keys rotating after every restart; an opt-in --data-dir with a stored state version; S3 object bodies on disk because all object bytes stay in RAM.

core/router/src/main.rs:185-187 constructs 'let engine: Arc<InMemoryEngine> = Arc::new(InMemoryEngine::new());' and builds one router from it; core/embedded/src/lib.rs:49 does the same per embedded emulator; README.md:70 describes each service's state.rs as 'this service's in-memory state'.
vendor/engine/src/lib.rs:103-118 — InMemoryEngine { states: Mutex<HashMap<TypeId, Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>>>, listeners } and new() allocating empty maps; no load/save API is defined.
vendor/server/src/cli.rs:20-32 (RunOptions fields) and :53-71 (complete USAGE) contain no --data-dir, snapshot or restore option; no env var for a state directory appears in vendor/server/src/lib.rs.

To start with empty state, restart the emulator.' 'Stopping the emulator': 'The emulator keeps all emulated resources in memory, so they're gone when it stops.' AWS Getting started with Docker: 'You lose the emulated resources, because the emulator keeps them in memory.'

findings.claim: AWS publishes no prebuilt image: the Docker guide makes every macOS, Windows and container-CI user build their own from an RPM ADD, with separate x86_64/aarch64 filenames and no signature verification. The repository ships no Dockerfile, no multi-arch manifest, no image build workflow and no CI sidecar guide. Community multi-arch images exist but are not official and drift from the published package.
findings.root_cause: The release channel publishes Linux RPM/DEB packages and a 'latest' alias only; the container path is documentation, not an artifact. Because the repo declines pull requests, community fixes (signature verification, multi-stage Dockerfile, buildah+cosign CI) cannot land in-tree.

findings.claim: The published version catalog's last entry is a four-component version (1.0.533.1 on 2026-11-19; 1.0.382.1 when gh#434 was filed), while the versioning guide's recipe substitutes that literal into package filenames whose working version is three components. Both literal Debian and RPM URLs return HTTP 403; dropping the final component returns 200; both latest aliases return 200. The documented version-pinning step is broken, so reproducible installs require guessing.
findings.root_cause: versions.json carries a fourth component that package filenames omit, while the guide states versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and says 'Replace <version> with a version from the list' without publishing any catalog-to-filename mapping. No catalog, checksum or mapping is tracked in the repository.
evidence: gh#434 (open, 'fix(packages): documented catalog versions produce inaccessible package URLs') reports the catalog entry {"productId":"aws-emulator","releaseStream":"LTS","version":"1.0.382.1"} and HEAD results: catalog literal Debian 403, RPM 403, shorter filename Debian 200, RPM 200, both latest aliases 200; an ordinary GET of the literal Debian URL also 403. Triage: P2, supported, workaround available (omit the final component), package contents untested.

AWS versioning guide (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/versioning.html): 'AWS Emulator versions use the format MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH'; 'Finding and installing a specific version' says 'Replace <version> with a version from the list' and gives the templates aws-emulator-<version>-1-x86_64.rpm, aws-emulator-<version>-1-aarch64.rpm, aws-emulator_<version>-1_amd64.deb and aws-emulator_<version>-1_arm64.deb. findings.claim: The emulator answers for every mounted service and CloudFormation resource type in any Region. There is no bundled per-Region availability snapshot, no EMULATOR_REGION_AVAILABILITY setting, and no router hook. gh#567 reports 7 concrete unavailable service/Region pairs (MemoryDB, Managed Grafana, EventBridge Pipes and AppSync in ap-southeast-6/ap-southeast-7) all accepted, including a CloudFormation stack reaching CREATE_COMPLETE, so code that passes locally fails at deploy.
findings.root_cause: The router registers all 440 service crates unconditionally and routes only on signing name/path; the CloudFormation type catalog is a flat &[&str] recognized with contains() and no Region parameter; SigV4 verification consumes the Region from the credential scope without validating it. The only Region allowlist in the tree is used to fold the telemetry environment.region dimension.
evidence: gh#567 (open, 'Refuse or warn when a template or call uses something AWS does not offer in that Region') gives the 7-pair Bangkok/Auckland table on 1.0.500, a grafana create-workspace repro, and asks for EMULATOR_REGION_AVAILABILITY=off|warn|enforce, a bundled daily-refreshed snapshot with a 30-day age warning, CreateStack/UpdateStack/CreateChangeSet refusals beginning 'Template format error: Unrecognized resource types: [...]', and one router hook in vendor/. It reports tested patches on a fork (trees ab9adbe806, 04cd5e326f, bb95e86ae9; 603 shared-crate tests, 364 unit + 1242 integration CloudFormation tests; 637 catalogued types across 37 Regions).

core/router/src/lib.rs:185 and :1010 are representative of build_router's unconditional register_service calls; vendor/smithy-server-runtime/src/multi_service_router.rs:17-25 (routing is signing-name/path only) and :53-70 (register_service takes no Region argument).

findings.claim: Telemetry is on by default and the config endpoint is compiled into both entry points as https://aws-emulator-telemetry.us-west-2.api.aws/v1/config. EMULATOR_TELEMETRY_CONFIG_ENDPOINT can override only toward the SAME host; there is no DO_NOT_TRACK support and no way to point telemetry at a self-hosted collector. A self-hosted substrate must explicitly opt out on every node or it will contact an AWS-owned endpoint by default.
findings.root_cause: policy::TELEMETRY_DEFAULT_ENABLED = true and TELEMETRY_CONSENT_MODE = OptOut; the standalone and embedded binaries inject an AWS endpoint constant; resolve_config_endpoint pins the env override with Endpoint::same_host; EMULATOR_TELEMETRY is the only env switch and DO_NOT_TRACK appears nowhere in the tracked tree.

findings.claim: Embedded mode defaults to authentication OFF and telemetry ON (the standalone binary defaults authentication ON), compiles all ~440 service crates with no Cargo feature gating, has no supported macOS/Windows build, and ships a dev profile that only reduces debug info. Telemetry is process-wide, so one instance's Telemetry::Off disables it for the whole test process and no later instance can re-enable it; embedded runs also write telemetry state into $HOME/.aws/emulator.

findings.claim: The shipped configuration surface is a single-process one: RunOptions has only telemetry, idle timeout, authentication, bind address and port, plus EMULATOR_BIND_ADDRESS and EMULATOR_DATA_PORT. There is no node identity, peer list, advertised endpoint, shared state backend, replica role, or node-aware readiness beyond one GET /__admin/health on the same HTTPS port. All identity (TLS CA, SigV4 keys, telemetry client) is process-global. A self-hosted multi-node substrate cannot be expressed with the shipped interface; it needs a cluster config plane before the other DX fixes can compose.
findings.root_cause: The binary constructs one InMemoryEngine, one router and one listener; TLS certificates, credentials and the telemetry client are OnceLock/AtomicBool globals; the health route reports only that the process bound its port.
evidence: vendor/server/src/cli.rs:20-32 (RunOptions = telemetry, idle_timeout, authentication, bind_address, port), :53-71 (complete USAGE: -b/-p/-h/-v/-t/-a/--idle-timeout), :93-116 (unknown arguments are rejected); vendor/server/src/lib.rs:1031 DATA_PORT_ENV = EMULATOR_DATA_PORT and :1059 BIND_ADDRESS_ENV = EMULATOR_BIND_ADDRESS are the only two listener env vars.

core/router/src/main.rs:104-121 sets the emulator home dir, parses args, sets the process-wide authentication AtomicBool and calls listen_on; :185-189 builds one InMemoryEngine, one router and one serve_emulator_until_shutdown call.
